artifacts.summary: Live-reproduced the ignored-specs commit defect (V7 refusal path, exit 2, can abort a legitimate sibling commit), confirmed the tracked-and-ignore-matching case needs no change, settled the per-repo-vs-per-pathspec predicate question (both), and designed a new V13 gate plus two new non-failure exit codes (8, 9) with the two other consumer sites needing case-arm updates.

memory_candidates.content: git check-ignore -q is index-aware in a way that makes it safe as a drop-classifier primitive for an untracked-but-ignored path WITHOUT a separate tracked/untracked test: it reliably reports 'not ignored' (rc=1) for any already-tracked path that merely matches a .gitignore rule, whether via a parent-directory pattern or a direct file-level rule, confirmed by live reproduction in both shapes.

Plain `git status --porcelain` (no --ignored flag) returns EMPTY output for an ignored, untracked path regardless of path argument -- a completeness/cleanliness check built on bare `git status --porcelain -- "$f"` is therefore already safe against a legitimately-ignored-and-never-committed path; no special-casing is needed at that layer.

In git-commit-scoped.sh's single all-or-nothing `git add <pathspecs...>` call, an ignored-and-untracked path does NOT poison the whole call the way an out-of-repository path does (V9): git add silently skips just the ignored entry and still stages the other, valid entries in the same call (confirmed: a mixed call with one ignored and one ordinary path staged the ordinary one, exit 1 overall). The fatal-whole-call poisoning is specific to the out-of-repository shape, not a general property of a 'git add partially fails' call.
